_comment: Scripted fake tracker/delivery responses for the fleet-ab umbrella (WF-405 slice: WF-406 + WF-409). Extends fixtures/fleet-two-task/project/fake-scripts.json's shape to a real backlog pair instead of synthetic FLEET- ids. Both children's descriptions are exported VERBATIM from Linear (fetched 2026-07-23) and were checked clean against the design doc's §6 banned-vocabulary list before being pasted here — no scrub edits were needed. seed-workspace.sh's blinding gate re-checks this file at seed time regardless (this comment included), so a future re-export can never silently reintroduce banned wording. Per the wf-fake tracker contract (capabilities/fake/fragments/tracker.ops.md): a scripted value that is a JSON ARRAY is an ordered sequence indexed by <call-index> = the count of PRIOR calls to that same (surface, op) pair (blind to args/id) — past the end the last element repeats. 'get' below is scripted as a 3-element sequence: element 0 for the umbrella's own 'get' (if the fleet/charter path resolves the umbrella by id before listing children), element 1 for the first child processed, element 2 for the second. Both orderings of WF-406/WF-409 are parallel-capable per the design doc, so either child may land on index 1 or 2 first at real run time — validate the exact call order against this fixture during the dry-run gate (design doc §8.2) before spending a measured run; if the observed order differs, reorder this array to match, never invent a fourth mechanism.

get.title: C021 slice — tracker mirror + constitution cleanup
get.description: A two-item backlog slice covering two independent, parallel-capable feature enhancements: mirroring one authoring phase to the tracker via declared slots, and composing a cleanup convention into the project's shared constitution payload plus a matching finalize-time sweep.

get.title: SUB-1 — Mirror the spec phase to the tracker via two slots
get.description:
Umbrella: C021 / WF-405 · Type: feat · Complexity: M · Depends on: — (first in the serialized SUB-1 -> SUB-2 -> SUB-3 chain) · Actor: tracker-bound developer / reviewer reading the tracker

Objective

At spec the tracker gets exactly one read plus one "Dev" backfill update and nothing else — no published spec artifact, and open questions never reach the parent. A team watching the tracker sees the task exist but cannot read its spec or its questions.

Deliver: after spec writes 01_spec.md in a Linear-bound project, the tracker carries the umbrella (created or reused) plus a Spec: sub-issue holding the full spec markdown (labelled, set Done as an artifact), and any open questions have been posted as a parent comment before the interactive questioning — with the existing single update reconciled, not duplicated.

Scope

In:
- Add interface.md to plugins/wf/skills/spec/ (none today) with a ## Slots section declaring spec.publish (merge policy replace) and spec.questions (replace).
- Insert <!-- wf:slot spec.publish --> (after 01_spec.md is written) and <!-- wf:slot spec.questions --> (before the interactive question block) markers in spec/SKILL.md, each with a no-op inline default.
- Contribute the spec.publish + spec.questions fragments in wf-linear (ensure umbrella create/reuse; publish Spec: sub-issue Done; post_comment open questions to the parent), bound only to abstract tracker-contract ops.
- Reconcile with spec's pre-existing single update (Dev backfill) — write per artifact, never double-publish.
- Version-bump wf core + wf-linear (both plugin.json + marketplace.json) and the top-level marketplace version.

Out: the plan/tasks slots (SUB-2); the implement slots (SUB-3); wf-ado fragments (SUB-4); the bare-core invariant test (SUB-5). Any tracker-contract extension — the five needed ops already exist; a genuinely missing op must be flagged loudly in the umbrella (WF-405), not added silently.

Success criteria (acceptance scenarios)

- Given a Linear-bound project and a task folder, when spec completes, then the tracker shows the umbrella plus a Spec: sub-issue containing the full spec markdown set to Done, and the Dev backfill update still runs exactly once (no duplicate spec write).
- Given open questions arise during spec, when the phase reaches its interactive question block, then those questions appear as a single parent comment on the umbrella before the user is prompted.
- Given the same run, when skill-slot-marker-lint.sh and validate-skill-interface (D1–D5) run against spec, then both pass and registry validation passes.

Constraints

Core purity (Article #1) — spec/SKILL.md names zero tracker nouns; all publish behavior lives in the wf-linear fragments behind the no-op defaults. Reuse the C014 slot mechanism exactly (## Slots declaration, <!-- wf:slot … --> markers, resolve_content class: slot under precedence _local/slots/spec.<point>.md > pack contribution > inline default), per capability-registry.ops.md §"Filled-slot resolution at runtime." Every change ships a version bump (§8); slot markers are CI-enforced.

Verification evidence

Live Linear end-to-end run showing umbrella + Spec: sub-issue + questions comment; slot lint + validate-skill-interface + registry validation all green; a single-write check confirming the spec item is written once per artifact.

get.title: SUB-6 — Compose cleanup articles into the constitution and sweep scratch at finalize
get.description:
Umbrella: C021 / WF-405 · Type: feat · Complexity: M · Depends on: — (parallel-capable; rebase-then-merge on shared version files) · Actor: any developer / reviewer relying on "nothing left behind"

Objective

The prototype's "nothing left behind" promise is unported: the constitution's scratch-placement article states only where scratch lives, with no lifecycle/sweep obligation, and tf leaves scratch residue behind at finalize.

Deliver: the constitution payload's scratch-placement article (core Article #9) is extended with a domain-free lifecycle clause stating both ported tmp-contract obligations explicitly — (a) per-consumer immediate deletion (each scratch file deleted the moment its consumer skill has run, not deferred to a later sweep) and (b) breadcrumb deletion by the run-ending skill — composed verbatim with core provenance; and tf sweeps scratch residue at finalize as the backstop for any residue those two obligations do not already remove, so no _local/scratch (.tmp) residue remains.

Scope

In:
- Extend core Article #9 in the constitution payload (the C015 mechanism) with a lifecycle clause stating both obligations explicitly (per-consumer immediate deletion + breadcrumb deletion by the run-ending skill), authored as a domain-free core process article, composed verbatim, with the tf finalize sweep named as the backstop, not a substitute for either obligation.
- Add a scratch sweep to plugins/wf/skills/tf/SKILL.md that removes any residual scratch at finalize (the backstop), obeying the "never write outside _local/" rule.
- Confirm /wf:constitution composes the new clause with core provenance.
- Version-bump wf core (constitution payload + tf) plus the top-level marketplace version.

Out: the seven bookkeeping slots (SUB-1/2/3); any tracker behavior; capability-authored articles (this clause is core, domain-free).

Success criteria (acceptance scenarios)

- Given a task with scratch residue under _local/scratch/, when tf finalizes, then no .tmp scratch residue remains and the sweep writes nothing outside _local/.
- Given /wf:constitution runs, when the constitution is composed, then the extended Article #9 clause appears verbatim with core provenance and states both obligations — per-consumer immediate deletion and breadcrumb deletion by the run-ending skill — with the tf finalize sweep named only as the backstop (the clause cannot pass while asserting a single vague sweep obligation).

Constraints

Cleanup articles are domain-free core process articles composed verbatim (C015 payload mechanism); the tf sweep obeys "never write outside _local/" (§6). Every change ships a version bump. Parallel-capable but rebase-then-merge on the shared wf-core version pair + top-level marketplace version.

Verification evidence

Post-run check showing no _local/scratch .tmp residue after tf; composed constitution showing the new clause under core provenance and carrying both obligations verbatim (per-consumer immediate deletion + breadcrumb deletion, tf sweep as backstop).
